\chapter{A Thief in the Night}
\label{ch:ml-a-thief-in-the-night}
\hlchaptermodality{364}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say a thief, a theft, a robbery, to steal and to break open.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 364: I can say a thief, a theft, a robbery, to steal and to break open.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കള്ളൻ} (kaḷḷan)}{കള്ളൻ (kaḷḷan)}]{\ml{കള്ളൻ} (kaḷḷan) — a thief}

\label{lesson:ML-C364-kallan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to explode, then the Malayalam for to collapse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കള്ളൻ}}
\textbf{\ml{കള്ളൻ}} — \emph{kaḷḷan} — \textquotedblleft{}a thief\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഇന്നലെ} \ml{രാത്രി} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{കള്ളൻ} \ml{ഞങ്ങളുടെ} \ml{വീട്ടിൽ} \ml{കയറി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{innale rātri oru kaḷḷan ñaṅṅaḷuṭe vīṭṭil kayaṟi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Last night a thief got into our house.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ml{കള്ളന്മാർ}, \emph{kaḷḷanmār}.

A woman thief is \ml{കള്ളി}. Also said, half in fun, of a cheeky child.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കള്ളൻ}} (\emph{kaḷḷan}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 1372 groups Malayalam \emph{kaḷḷan}, \textquotedblleft{}thief, liar, rogue\textquotedblright{}, with Tamil \emph{kaḷ}, \textquotedblleft{}to steal\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaḷḷan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaḷḷan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{innale rātri oru kaḷḷan ñaṅṅaḷuṭe vīṭṭil kayaṟi.} — Last night a thief got into our house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to explode, then the Malayalam for to collapse, then say \emph{kaḷḷan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കള്ളൻ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A thief\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മോഷണം} (mōṣaṇaṁ)}{മോഷണം (mōṣaṇaṁ)}]{\ml{മോഷണം} (mōṣaṇaṁ) — a theft}

\label{lesson:ML-C364-mosanam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to collapse, then the Malayalam for a thief.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മോഷണം}}
\textbf{\ml{മോഷണം}} — \emph{mōṣaṇaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}a theft\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ബാങ്കിലെ} \ml{മോഷണം} \ml{പത്രത്തിൽ} \ml{വാർത്തയായി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bāṅkile mōṣaṇaṁ patrattil vārttayāyi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The theft at the bank was in the news.
\end{quote}

The formal word; in speech people often say \ml{കളവ്}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{മോഷണം}} (\emph{mōṣaṇaṁ}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{moṣaṇa}, \textquotedblleft{}robbing, plundering; the act of robbing\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mōṣaṇaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mōṣaṇaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāṅkile mōṣaṇaṁ patrattil vārttayāyi.} — The theft at the bank was in the news.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to collapse, then the Malayalam for a thief, then say \emph{mōṣaṇaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{മോഷണം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A theft\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കവർച്ച} (kavarcca)}{കവർച്ച (kavarcca)}]{\ml{കവർച്ച} (kavarcca) — a robbery}

\label{lesson:ML-C364-kavarcca}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a thief, then the Malayalam for a theft.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കവർച്ച}}
\textbf{\ml{കവർച്ച}} — \emph{kavarcca} — \textquotedblleft{}a robbery\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{കവലയിലെ} \ml{കടയിൽ} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{കവർച്ച} \ml{നടന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kavalayile kaṭayil oru kavarcca naṭannu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A robbery took place at the shop at the junction.
\end{quote}

A robbery takes place: \ml{കവർച്ച} \ml{നടന്നു}. Stronger than a theft: someone takes by force.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കവർച്ച}} (\emph{kavarcca}) is native Dravidian, the noun of \ml{കവരുക} (\emph{kavaruka}), \textquotedblleft{}to plunder, to rob\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1326), which DEDR sets beside Tamil \emph{kavar}, \textquotedblleft{}to seize, to grasp\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kavarcca}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kavarcca}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kavalayile kaṭayil oru kavarcca naṭannu.} — A robbery took place at the shop at the junction.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a thief, then the Malayalam for a theft, then say \emph{kavarcca} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കവർച്ച} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A robbery\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മോഷ്ടിക്കുക} (mōṣṭikkuka)}{മോഷ്ടിക്കുക (mōṣṭikkuka)}]{\ml{മോഷ്ടിക്കുക} (mōṣṭikkuka) — to steal}

\label{lesson:ML-C364-mostikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a theft, then the Malayalam for a robbery.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മോഷ്ടിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{മോഷ്ടിക്കുക}} — \emph{mōṣṭikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to steal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{കള്ളൻ} \ml{അമ്മയുടെ} \ml{സ്വർണ്ണം} \ml{മോഷ്ടിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kaḷḷan ammayuṭe svarṇṇaṁ mōṣṭiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief stole mother's gold.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{മോഷ്ടിച്ചു}, \emph{mōṣṭiccu}.

What is stolen is the plain object; from whom takes -\ml{ഇൽ} \ml{നിന്ന്}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{മോഷ്ടിക്കുക}} (\emph{mōṣṭikkuka}) is built from the same Sanskrit verb as \ml{മോഷണം}, \emph{muṣ}, \textquotedblleft{}to rob\textquotedblright{}, whose noun \emph{moṣaṇa} means \textquotedblleft{}robbing\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the Malayalam verb ending -\ml{ിക്കുക}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mōṣṭikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mōṣṭikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaḷḷan ammayuṭe svarṇṇaṁ mōṣṭiccu.} — The thief stole mother's gold.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a theft, then the Malayalam for a robbery, then say \emph{mōṣṭikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{മോഷ്ടിക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To steal\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കുത്തിത്തുറക്കുക} (kuttittuṟakkuka)}{കുത്തിത്തുറക്കുക (kuttittuṟakkuka)}]{\ml{കുത്തിത്തുറക്കുക} (kuttittuṟakkuka) — to break open}

\label{lesson:ML-C364-kuttitturakkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a robbery, then the Malayalam for to steal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കുത്തിത്തുറക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{കുത്തിത്തുറക്കുക}} — \emph{kuttittuṟakkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to break open\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{കള്ളന്മാർ} \ml{രാത്രി} \ml{കടയുടെ} \ml{പൂട്ട്} \ml{കുത്തിത്തുറന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kaḷḷanmār rātri kaṭayuṭe pūṭṭŭ kuttittuṟannu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thieves broke open the shop's lock at night.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{കുത്തിത്തുറന്നു}, \emph{kuttittuṟannu}.

\ml{കുത്തുക}, to pierce, + \ml{തുറക്കുക}, to open: to force a door or a lock.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കുത്തിത്തുറക്കുക}} (\emph{kuttittuṟakkuka}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{കുത്തുക} (\emph{kuttuka}), \textquotedblleft{}to pierce, to stab\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1719), and \ml{തുറക്കുക} (\emph{tuṟakkuka}), \textquotedblleft{}to open\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3259): to open by forcing a point in.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuttittuṟakkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuttittuṟakkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaḷḷanmār rātri kaṭayuṭe pūṭṭŭ kuttittuṟannu.} — The thieves broke open the shop's lock at night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a robbery, then the Malayalam for to steal, then say \emph{kuttittuṟakkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കുത്തിത്തുറക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To break open\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 357–364 — a review}

\label{lesson:ML-R364-review-357-364}



\begin{quote}
Say the Malayalam for afterwards and gradually.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item afterwards, gradually, until then, ever since, all of a sudden
  \item once upon a time, in those days, at that moment, following that, throughout
  \item before long, in the end, nearly, now and then, right after
  \item by chance, on purpose, a blunder, luck, as fate willed
  \item an era, the past, an occasion, a beginning, unexpectedly
  \item a fire, the fire brigade, ashes, to catch fire, to burn down
  \item a flame, damage, to blaze up, to explode, to collapse
  \item a thief, a theft, a robbery, to steal, to break open
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Afterwards? (\textbf{\ml{പിന്നീട്}}, \emph{pinnīṭŭ}.) Gradually? (\textbf{\ml{ക്രമേണ}}, \emph{kramēṇa}.) Until then? (\textbf{\ml{അതുവരെ}}, \emph{atuvare}.) Ever since? (\textbf{\ml{അന്നുമുതൽ}}, \emph{annumutal}.) All of a sudden? (\textbf{\ml{പൊടുന്നനെ}}, \emph{poṭunnane}.) Once upon a time? (\textbf{\ml{പണ്ടുപണ്ട്}}, \emph{paṇṭupaṇṭŭ}.) In those days? (\textbf{\ml{അക്കാലത്ത്}}, \emph{akkālattŭ}.) At that moment? (\textbf{\ml{അന്നേരം}}, \emph{annēraṁ}.) Following that? (\textbf{\ml{തുടർന്ന്}}, \emph{tuṭarnnŭ}.) Throughout? (\textbf{\ml{ഉടനീളം}}, \emph{uṭanīḷaṁ}.) Before long? (\textbf{\ml{വൈകാതെ}}, \emph{vaikāte}.) In the end? (\textbf{\ml{ഒടുക്കം}}, \emph{oṭukkaṁ}.) Nearly? (\textbf{\ml{ഏതാണ്ട്}}, \emph{ētāṇṭŭ}.) Now and then? (\textbf{\ml{ഇടയ്ക്കിടെ}}, \emph{iṭaykkiṭe}.) Right after? (\textbf{\ml{തൊട്ടുപിന്നാലെ}}, \emph{toṭṭupinnāle}.) By chance? (\textbf{\ml{യാദൃച്ഛികമായി}}, \emph{yādṛcchikamāyi}.) On purpose? (\textbf{\ml{മനപ്പൂർവം}}, \emph{manappūrvaṁ}.) A blunder? (\textbf{\ml{അബദ്ധം}}, \emph{abaddhaṁ}.) Luck? (\textbf{\ml{ഭാഗ്യം}}, \emph{bhāgyaṁ}.) As fate willed? (\textbf{\ml{വിധിവശാൽ}}, \emph{vidhivaśāl}.) An era? (\textbf{\ml{യുഗം}}, \emph{yugaṁ}.) The past? (\textbf{\ml{ഭൂതകാലം}}, \emph{bhūtakālaṁ}.) An occasion? (\textbf{\ml{സന്ദർഭം}}, \emph{sandarbhaṁ}.) A beginning? (\textbf{\ml{തുടക്കം}}, \emph{tuṭakkaṁ}.) Unexpectedly? (\textbf{\ml{അപ്രതീക്ഷിതമായി}}, \emph{apratīkṣitamāyi}.) A fire? (\textbf{\ml{തീപിടിത്തം}}, \emph{tīpiṭittaṁ}.) The fire brigade? (\textbf{\ml{അഗ്നിശമനസേന}}, \emph{agniśamanasēna}.) Ashes? (\textbf{\ml{ചാമ്പൽ}}, \emph{cāmpal}.) To catch fire? (\textbf{\ml{തീപിടിക്കുക}}, \emph{tīpiṭikkuka}.) To burn down? (\textbf{\ml{കത്തിനശിക്കുക}}, \emph{kattinaśikkuka}.) A flame? (\textbf{\ml{ജ്വാല}}, \emph{jvāla}.) Damage? (\textbf{\ml{നാശനഷ്ടം}}, \emph{nāśanaṣṭaṁ}.) To blaze up? (\textbf{\ml{ആളിക്കത്തുക}}, \emph{āḷikkattuka}.) To explode? (\textbf{\ml{പൊട്ടിത്തെറിക്കുക}}, \emph{poṭṭitteṟikkuka}.) To collapse? (\textbf{\ml{തകരുക}}, \emph{takaruka}.) A thief? (\textbf{\ml{കള്ളൻ}}, \emph{kaḷḷan}.) A theft? (\textbf{\ml{മോഷണം}}, \emph{mōṣaṇaṁ}.) A robbery? (\textbf{\ml{കവർച്ച}}, \emph{kavarcca}.) To steal? (\textbf{\ml{മോഷ്ടിക്കുക}}, \emph{mōṣṭikkuka}.) To break open? (\textbf{\ml{കുത്തിത്തുറക്കുക}}, \emph{kuttittuṟakkuka}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
